extracted.intended_audience: The people of the State of New York; citizens/voters considering ratification of the proposed Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: A series of political essays arguing for adoption of the proposed federal Constitution by explaining the practical advantages of a national Union (revenue, economy, defense, commerce, and governability) and rebutting objections about extent and the insufficiency of the Confederation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union as best means to raise revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as this would be conducive to the interests of commerce, so far it must tend to the extension of the revenue to be drawn from that source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union allows duties and imposts to be applied more extensively and effectively than separate States; consolidating revenue sources under one government increases productive capacity of given duties and permits higher rates without prejudicing trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on indirect taxation (duties/imposts)
rubrics_metrics.description: In America, it is evident that we must a long time depend for the means of revenue chiefly on such duties. In most parts of it, excises must be confined within a narrow compass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because direct taxation (land, personal property) is politically and practically limited, the principal sustainable revenue source is taxes on consumption (imports, duties). Policy should acknowledge popular resistance to excises and the difficulty of tracing personal estate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union reduces illicit inter-state trade and evasion of customs
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative situation of these States ... the facility of communication ... would conspire to render an illicit trade between them a matter of little difficulty, and would insure frequent evasions of the commercial regulations of each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate states would be tempted to low duties to prevent smuggling, but a single government reduces internal avenues for contraband and makes enforcement of commercial regulations practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrated enforcement on external frontier (Atlantic coast)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there be but one government pervading all the States, there will be, as to the principal part of our commerce, but ONE SIDE to guard--the ATLANTIC COAST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government can focus resources (a few armed vessels, stationed at port entrances) to guard imports effectively at lower expense than multiple internal patrols required by disunion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific duties (example: ardent spirits) to raise revenue and promote public good
rubrics_metrics.description: The single article of ardent spirits, under federal regulation, might be made to furnish a considerable revenue... at a shilling per gallon, would produce two hundred thousand pounds. That article would well bear this rate of duty; and if it should tend to diminish the consumption of it, such an effect would be equally favorable to the agriculture, to the economy, to the morals, and to the health of the society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative calculation: targeted import duties can produce substantial revenue and incidental social benefits; such measures are more feasible under federal regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of revenue for national existence
rubrics_metrics.description: A nation cannot long exist without revenues. Destitute of this essential support, it must resign its independence, and sink into the degraded condition of a province.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequate, enforceable revenue sources are essential for national sovereignty, public credit, and defense; failure to secure revenue jeopardizes independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy through a single national civil list
rubrics_metrics.description: If the States are united under one government, there will be but one national civil list to support; if they are divided into several confederacies, there will be as many different national civil lists to be provided for--and each of them, as to the principal departments, coextensive with that which would be necessary for a government of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union saves money by avoiding duplicate national administrations; multiple confederacies create redundant executive/administrative expenditures that negate claimed savings from smaller governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into confederacies increases defensive and enforcement costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in addition to the consideration of a plurality of civil lists, we take into view the number of persons who must necessarily be employed to guard the inland communication between the different confederacies against illicit trade, and ... the military establishments which it has been shown would unavoidably result from the jealousies and conflicts of the several nations ... a separation would be not less injurious to the economy, than to the tranquillity, commerce, revenue, and liberty of every part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmentation leads to proliferation of internal guards, customs forces, and standing militaries, increasing expense and endangering liberty and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of an extended republic (representative government vs democracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true distinction between these forms was also adverted to on a former occasion. It is, that in a democracy, the people meet and exercise the government in person; in a republic, they assemble and administer it by their representatives and agents. A democracy, consequently, will be confined to a small spot. A republic may be extended over a large region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extended territory is compatible with republican government because representation, not personal participation, governs; thus objections based on extent confuse democracy with republic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited federal jurisdiction mitigates difficulties of distance
rubrics_metrics.description: The general government is not to be charged with the whole power of making and administering laws. Its jurisdiction is limited to certain enumerated objects ... The subordinate governments ... will retain their due authority and activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because many matters remain with state governments, the national government need not be omnipresent; this division of labor reduces problems arising from geographic extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements in infrastructure will ease intercourse across extent
rubrics_metrics.description: The intercourse throughout the Union will be facilitated by new improvements. Roads will everywhere be shortened, and kept in better order; accommodations for travelers will be multiplied and meliorated; an interior navigation ... will be opened ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated internal improvements (roads, canals, navigation) will reduce effective distances and make governance of an extended republic more practicable over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frontier states derive special security benefits from the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: As almost every State will, on one side or other, be a frontier ... the States which lie at the greatest distance from the heart of the Union ... will be at the same time immediately contiguous to foreign nations, and will consequently stand, on particular occasions, in greatest need of its strength and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if distant states receive fewer peacetime benefits, they gain greater defensive protection and resources from the Union, balancing equities across the country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confederation's radical defect: legislation for States rather than individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: The great and radical vice in the construction of the existing Confederation is in the principle of LEGISLATION for STATES or GOVERNMENTS, in their CORPORATE or COLLECTIVE CAPACITIES, and as contradistinguished from the INDIVIDUALS of which they consist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national government must be able to legislate directly upon individuals (e.g., to raise men and money); reliance on requisitions to States renders national laws unenforceable and makes resolutions mere recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-style treaties/alliances are inadequate substitutes for a government with coercive powers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing absurd or impracticable in the idea of a league or alliance between independent nations ... leaving nothing to future discretion; and depending for its execution on the good faith of the parties. ... from which the politicians of the times fondly hoped for benefits which were never realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leagues and treaties lack the continuous, coercive authority of a single government and therefore cannot reliably secure the public ends (revenue, defense, enforcement) that a national government can.
